title: Analysis of mouse intestinal organoid culture with conditioned media from enteric glial cells
author: Baghdadi, Kim
materials:
Timing: 7–8 h
CRITICAL: RNA molecules are highly sensitive to degradation. To isolate intact, high-quality RNA, it is essential that RNases are not introduced throughout the RNA extraction procedure. Decontaminate pipettors, benchtops, centrifuge, and ice bucket with a surface decontamination solution like RNAse Away®, and use RNAse-free tips, tubes, PBS 1× and H20. In addition, the whole procedure should be done fast to avoid RNA degradation.
70.Following step 69, remove media from organoid culture and add 400 μL of ice-cold PBS 1× per well. Incubate the plate on ice for 5 min.71.Break up the Matrigel-organoid dome by pipetting up and down.
Note: To avoid bubbles, set the pipette at 250 μL.
72.Pool two wells into a 15 mL conical tube filled with 5 mL of ice-cold PBS 1×. Pipette up and down with a 1,000 μL pipette 15 times to further dissociate the Matrigel.
Note: For solid statistical analysis, we recommend to pool 2 wells for one qPCR data point and use 3 data points per mouse and/or condition.
73.Centrifuge at 150 g for 10 min at 4°C.74.Carefully discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 350 μL of Qiagen RLT buffer supplemented with 1% β-mercaptoethanol.
CRITICAL: β-mercaptoethanol is toxic and should be used in the fume hood.
75.Vortex the tubes for 30 s to fully lyse the organoids.76.Spin the tubes at 150 g for 1 min at 4°C.
Pause point: At this step, the lysate can be transferred to a RNAse-free 1.5 mL tube, snap frozen in dry ice and kept at −80°C until ready for RNA extraction.
77.Proceed with the Qiagen RNeasy® Plus Mini extraction kit according to the manufacturers’ instructions: https://www.qiagen.com/us/resources/download.aspx?id=14e7cf6e-521a-4cf7-8cbc-bf9f6fa33e24&lang=en.
Pause point: RNA can be kept at −80°C until ready for the reverse transcription step.
78.Measure RNA yield and concentration with a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.a.For an optimal amplification, use ≤ 50 ng of RNA for one qPCR well.b.Transfer the necessary quantity of RNA in a clean RNAse-free 1.5 mL tube.c.Perform reverse transcription according to manufacturers’ guidelines: https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.thermofisher.com%2FTFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2FsuperscriptIII_man.pdf.
Pause point: cDNA can be stored at −80°C until ready to load qPCR plate.
79.Run qPCR following manufacturers’ instructions: https://www.thermofisher.com/document-connect/document-connect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fassets.thermofisher.com%2FTFS-Assets%2FLSG%2Fmanuals%2Fcms_042179.pdf.
Note: For 1 qPCR well: Mix 5 μL of SYBR green master mix + 4 μL cDNA + 1 μL primer mix (forward + reverse at 10 μM).
CRITICAL: Load qPCR plate on ice.
80.Analyze data using the 2-ΔΔCT method (Livak and Schmittgen, 2001). We recommend the use of two independent genes for expression normalization. First normalize the gene of interest with each housekeeping gene separately and perform the mean value of both to obtain the final 2-ΔΔCT value.
Note: Specific forward and reverse primers for commonly used crypt population markers are listed in Table 1. Tbp and Rpl13 are normalization housekeeping genes.

steps.title: Euthanize and sterilize mouse
steps.instruction: Euthanize mice using an authorized, legal method and sterilize the abdomen with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dissect gut into ice‑cold buffer
steps.instruction: Make a midline abdominal incision, lift the liver, cut the intestine at the pyloric sphincter and across the large intestine, pull the gut out, and place it in a petri dish filled with ice‑cold gut buffer.

steps.title: Remove mesentery, separate intestine, flush feces
steps.instruction: Tear away the mesentery to unfold the gut, cut at the ileocecal junction to separate small intestine from colon, and flush the intestinal lumen with ice‑cold gut buffer using a 1 mL syringe fitted with a 1,000 µL tip (use forceps if needed).

steps.title: Segment, open, and scrape villi
steps.instruction: Cut the intestine into three equal pieces (duodenum, jejunum, ileum), open each segment longitudinally with the lumen facing up, and gently scrape off the villi with a slide, discarding the remaining lumen material.

steps.title: Wash segments in gut buffer
steps.instruction: Place the intestinal segments in a 50 mL conical tube containing 20 mL ice‑cold gut buffer, invert gently three times, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Chelate tissue pieces
steps.instruction: Cut the segments into 0.5 cm pieces, transfer them to a 15 mL tube with 10 mL ice‑cold chelating buffer, and shake at 20 rpm for 25 min at 4 °C (fridge or cold‑room).

steps.title: Filter chelation suspension
steps.instruction: Gently invert the tube and filter the solution through a 100 µm strainer into a fresh 50 mL conical tube to separate tissue pieces from cellular debris.

steps.title: Dissociate crypts mechanically
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue pieces to a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL ice‑cold crypt dissociation buffer, orient the tube at 45°, and shake for 4–6 min with a gentle regular motion, placing the tube on ice for 30 s every 2 min.

steps.title: Check crypt enrichment
steps.instruction: Pipet 50 µL of the suspension, examine under a microscope for crypt enrichment; if insufficient, shake an additional 2 min and re‑check.

steps.title: Filter to enrich crypts
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice to let fragments settle, then filter the suspension through a 70 µm filter into a 50 mL conical tube kept on ice.

steps.title: Wash filter and discard strainer
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL crypt dissociation buffer to the 70 µm strainer, wash, and discard the strainer.

steps.title: Centrifuge crypt suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the crypt‑containing solution at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend crypt pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant carefully and resuspend the crypt pellet in 10 mL ice‑cold PBS 1×.

steps.title: Count and aliquot crypts
steps.instruction: Count crypts in 10 µL; total crypts = count × 1,000. Transfer the volume containing 300 crypts per well (7,200 crypts for a full 24‑well plate) to a new 15 mL tube. If the count is too high, dilute the suspension with an extra 10 mL ice‑cold PBS 1× before counting.

steps.title: Centrifuge aliquoted crypts
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the required number of crypts at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Euthanize and dissect for EGCs
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 1–3 (euthanize, sterilize abdomen, dissect gut, place in ice‑cold gut buffer) for the enteric glial cell isolation.

steps.title: Remove mesentery and flush for EGCs
steps.instruction: Tear away mesentery, separate small intestine from colon, and flush fecal content with ice‑cold gut buffer using a 1 mL syringe with a 1,000 µL tip.

steps.title: Remove longitudinal muscle
steps.instruction: Cut the intestine into three pieces, soak the wooden part of a cotton swab in cold gut buffer, thread one segment onto the stick, make vertical incisions with a scalpel, and gently tease away the longitudinal muscle using the pre‑wetted swab until the muscle peels off; discard the muscle. Repeat for the remaining segments.

steps.title: Initial EGC tissue digestion
steps.instruction: Cut the cleaned intestinal pieces into 0.5 cm fragments and transfer them to a 50 mL tube containing 25 mL ice‑cold EGC isolation solution; shake gently for 15 min at 4 °C (fridge or cold‑room).

steps.title: Triturate tissue (first round)
steps.instruction: Pipette the tissue‑solution mixture up and down 20 times with a moistened 10 mL plastic pipette to further dissociate the tissue.

steps.title: Filter and repeat digestion
steps.instruction: Filter the mixture through a 100 µm strainer into a new 50 mL tube; repeat the transfer, shaking, trituration, and filtration steps three times or until the solution becomes clear.

steps.title: Cell recovery incubation
steps.instruction: Transfer the tissue pieces to a 15 mL tube with 10 mL Corning Cell Recovery solution and rock for 30 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Second trituration and fine filtration
steps.instruction: Triturate the suspension with a moistened 5 mL pipette (20 passes), filter through a 40 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube, and discard the remaining tissue pieces.

steps.title: Wash filter and collect cells
steps.instruction: Wash the 40 µm strainer with 2 mL cold PBS 1×, collect the flow‑through into a 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge EGC suspension
steps.instruction: Spin at 2,000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend and plate EGCs
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL EGC culture media and plate 330 µL of this suspension together with 170 µL fresh EGC media per well of a PDL‑ and laminin‑coated 12‑well plate (three wells total).

steps.title: Remove non‑adherent cells
steps.instruction: After 24 h, gently pipette off the medium containing non‑adherent stromal cells, rinse wells with PBS 1×, and add fresh pre‑warmed EGC culture media.

steps.title: Culture duration before use
steps.instruction: Use the cultured mucosal enteric glial cells for experiments 3–4 days after plating.

steps.title: Prepare organoids for RNA extraction
steps.instruction: Remove organoid media, add 400 µL ice‑cold PBS 1× per well, and incubate the plate on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Disrupt Matrigel domes
steps.instruction: Break up each Matrigel‑organoid dome by pipetting up and down (set pipette to 250 µL).

steps.title: Pool and further dissociate
steps.instruction: Pool two wells into a 15 mL conical tube containing 5 mL ice‑cold PBS 1× and pipette up and down 15 times with a 1,000 µL pipette to further dissociate the Matrigel.

steps.title: Centrifuge organoid lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Lyse organoids in RLT buffer
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 350 µL Qiagen RLT buffer supplemented with 1 % β‑mercaptoethanol (handle in a fume hood). Vortex 30 s, then spin at 150 g for 1 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Extract total RNA
steps.instruction: Proceed with the Qiagen RNeasy® Plus Mini kit according to the manufacturer’s instructions; lysates may be snap‑frozen at –80 °C if extraction is delayed.

steps.title: Quantify RNA and reverse transcribe
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration with a Nanodrop, use ≤50 ng RNA per qPCR well, transfer the required amount to a clean RNase‑free tube, and perform reverse transcription following the kit’s protocol (cDNA can be stored at –80 °C).

steps.title: Run qPCR
steps.instruction: Set up qPCR reactions on ice: 5 µL SYBR Green master mix + 4 µL cDNA + 1 µL primer mix (10 µM each). Run the qPCR according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data
steps.instruction: Calculate relative expression using the 2‑ΔΔCT method, normalizing each target gene to two housekeeping genes (e.g., Tbp and Rpl13) and averaging the two results.

steps.title: Prepare organoids for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm 5 mL TrypLe 1× at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash organoids with PBS
steps.instruction: Remove media, add 400 µL ice‑cold PBS 1× per well, and incubate on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Disrupt Matrigel domes (flow)
steps.instruction: Break up the Matrigel‑organoid domes by pipetting up and down (250 µL setting).

steps.title: Pool wells and further dissociate
steps.instruction: Pool all wells for one mouse/condition into a 15 mL tube with 3 mL ice‑cold PBS 1× and pipette up and down 15 times to further dissociate the Matrigel.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 150 g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Enzymatic dissociation with TrypLe
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL pre‑warmed TrypLe 1× and incubate at 37 °C for 3 min.

steps.title: Mechanical trituration
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 5 mL syringe equipped with an 18 G blunt needle 15 times to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

steps.title: Neutralize TrypLe
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL cold gut buffer to neutralize the TrypLe.

steps.title: Wash and resuspend cells
steps.instruction: Spin at 400 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL gut buffer.

steps.title: Stain with antibodies and viability dye
steps.instruction: Set aside 50 µL of the cell suspension as a GFP‑only control. Add to the remaining 500 µL: CD24‑Pacific Blue (1 µL, 1/500), EPCAM‑APC (1 µL, 1/500), and propidium iodide (0.5 µL, 1/1000). Incubate 20 min on ice in the dark.

steps.title: Wash stained cells
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL gut buffer, spin at 400 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL gut buffer.

steps.title: Acquire flow cytometry data
steps.instruction: Run the samples on a flow cytometer, using the GFP‑only control to set parameters, and analyze gating as described (exclude doublets, dead cells, then identify CD24Low/Med + SSC Low/Med EPCAM⁺ Lgr5‑GFP⁺ cells as ISCs).
